headline: DC Nonprofit Breaks Ground on $30M Hub for Medical Meals
meta_description: A Washington DC nonprofit delivering over 2 million medically tailored meals annually to patients with serious illnesses begins construction on a $30 million f…
summary_short: A Washington DC nonprofit that serves patients with cancer, AIDS, and renal failure has broken ground on a major $30 million expansion project.
body:
A Washington DC nonprofit has broken ground on a $30 million facility to expand its mission of delivering medically tailored meals to patients battling serious illnesses.

The organization currently delivers more than 2 million meals each year to people living with cancer, AIDS, renal failure, and other critical health conditions. These meals are specially prepared to meet the medical and nutritional needs of patients whose illnesses make standard diets inadequate or harmful.

The new construction represents a significant scaling of the nonprofit's reach and capacity. By expanding its infrastructure, the organization aims to serve even more vulnerable patients who depend on nutrition as part of their medical treatment—acknowledging what evidence increasingly shows: that food itself can be medicine when carefully matched to a patient's specific condition.
